newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends firm despite dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends firm despite dlr demand.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed a shade firmer despite import covering, because demand for the U.S. unit was filled without disturbing the market, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 56.72 after opening at 56.74, which was higher than its previous closing level of 56.77, they said.
"The dollar fell to 56.68 when the Central Bank left the exchange rate unchanged, but gained ground on import covering by a state bank," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
"The disciplined manner in which the bank covered its imports, prevented the dollar from rising sharply," he said.
Overnight call money closed at 16 percent after opening at 17, with the market liquid, dealers said.
They expect call rates to fall further since lenders of Thursday money are at 17 percent while borrowers are at 14.
